body_ar:
حكم استئذان حاكم المقاطعة في إقامة الجمعة

ما قولكم في أهل قرية وجبت عليهم الجمعة فابتدأوا إقامتها في قريتهم هذه إلا أنهم صلوا ثلاث جمع قبل استئذان حاكم المقاطعة التي يتبعون لها؟

أن الصلاة فريضة افترضها الله تعالى على عباده وهي الصلة بين العبد وربه وهي حق الله المتمحض فلا يستشار فيها أحد، كما لا يستشار الحاكم في إقامة صلاة الصبح ولا صلاة الظهر ولا صلاة العصر ولا صلاة المغرب ولا صلاة العشاء، كذلك لا يستأمر في صلاة الجمعة فلا فرق فهي فرض يومها، فإن الله افترضها على محمد (ص) وهو بمكة قبل الهجرة ولم يكن يستطيع أداءها بمكة، فصلاها أصحابه بالمدينة ..
body_en:
The ruling on seeking the permission of the district governor for holding the Friday prayer

What do you say about the people of a village upon whom the Friday prayer had become obligatory, who began to hold it in this village of theirs, except that they prayed three Friday prayers before seeking the permission of the governor of the district to which they belong?

The prayer is an obligation which God, exalted, made obligatory upon His servants. It is the bond between the servant and his Lord, and it is a right belonging purely to God, so no one is consulted about it. Just as the governor is not consulted about holding the dawn prayer, nor the noon prayer, nor the afternoon prayer, nor the sunset prayer, nor the night prayer, so likewise his authorisation is not sought for the Friday prayer. There is no difference: it is the obligation of its day. For God made it obligatory upon Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, while he was in Mecca before the emigration, and he was not able to perform it in Mecca, so his Companions prayed it in Medina ..

flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY — STYLE GUIDE §9 AND §10. The question has two parts: whether permission must be sought, and what the standing of the three Friday prayers already performed is. The page breaks off, on a double full stop, in the middle of the historical argument and before the second part is answered at all. A reader is left with a ruling that no permission is needed and no word on the prayers already prayed, which is the practical question the villagers actually asked. The record's title also promises general fatwas on prayer in the plural, and only this one is present. The full answer is behind the .docx download.

flags.arabic: وهي حق الله المتمحض فلا يستشار فيها أحد
flags.context: the Sheikh's ruling on whether state permission is required for the Friday prayer
options: render literally: it is a right belonging purely to God, so no one is consulted about it
render with the political edge softened
render with an added qualification about local law
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW. This is a ruling that the permission of the civil authority is not required for a congregational obligation, delivered in a setting where the authorisation of mosques is a matter of state control. Read in English out of that setting it is a statement about religious practice and state authority, and in some jurisdictions it carries obvious weight. It has been translated faithfully, neither softened nor strengthened, and no qualification the Sheikh did not give has been added. The publication decision belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office. Note too that the argument is truncated before its conclusion, so what the Sheikh does with this premise is not visible.

flags.context: the official whose permission is in question
flags.note: muqāṭaʿah is the Mauritanian administrative division, rendered in the country's French administrative vocabulary as a département and headed by a hākim. 'District governor' is the nearest plain-English handle but loses the specificity of the office. A reviewer familiar with Mauritanian administrative terminology should fix the rendering, as the term will recur.

EXCERPT ONLY. The page publishes the opening and breaks off; the full text sits behind the .docx download recorded in source_download_link. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends and the thought has not been completed. The site must render this with an excerpt banner, never as a whole article.
The first line of the body is a sub-heading in the source rather than part of the question; it has been kept as the source has it.

'It is the obligation of its day' renders fa-hiya farḍ yawmihā: the Friday prayer is the obligatory prayer of that day, standing in place of the noon prayer. The Sheikh states this compactly and it has not been expanded.

The historical claim that the Friday prayer was made obligatory in Mecca before the emigration is the Sheikh's own and is given without evidence in the published text; nothing has been added to support or qualify it.
